mainTopic: Waving the לולב, interrupting a meal to take the לולב, and being led in הלל by others
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching about תנופה (waving). Even a non-essential part of a מצוה holds back harm, and רבא says the same is true of waving the לולב. רב אחא בר יעקב used to call his waving 'an arrow in the eye of the שטן', but the גמרא says boasting like this only provokes the שטן. Next, a משנה teaches that a traveler without a לולב takes it at his table when he gets home, and someone who missed the morning may take it in the afternoon, since the whole day is valid. The גמרא asks whether this means one must stop a meal for the לולב, which seems to clash with the rule that one does not stop a meal for תפילה. רב ספרא answers that one interrupts only when no time is left in the day. רבא and רבי זירא then debate which contradiction is the real one. רבי זירא concludes that the משנה is about the later days of סוכות, when the לולב is only rabbinic, and he proves this from the fact that the משנה describes a traveler. A new משנה then discusses being led in הלל by an עבד, an אשה, or a קטן, and says that the form of הלל follows local custom. A ברייתא adds that a man who relies on his wife and children to say a ברכה for him deserves a curse, and a statement of רבא begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Extra parts of a מצוה hold back disaster
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of a teaching: שיירי מצוה, the non-essential add-ons of a מצוה, prevent calamity, as shown by תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leftover, non-essential parts of a מצוה hold back punishment. After all, waving is a non-essential part of the מצוה, and yet it stops harmful winds and harmful dews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started on the previous amud. Even the 'extra' parts of a מצוה have real power to protect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה (waving the offering) is not required: if it was skipped, the מצוה still counts. Even so, it stops harmful winds and dews. From this the speaker concludes that all שיירי מצוה protect against פורענות.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'leftovers' of a מצוה: parts that are not essential to fulfilling it
Waving (of an offering, or of the לולב)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'non-essential' means 'unimportant'. The point is the opposite: even the optional part of a מצוה has protective power.

phrases.english: The non-essential parts of a מצוה hold back calamity.
For waving is a non-essential part of the מצוה,
phrases.notes: If one did not wave, he still fulfilled the מצוה.

phrases.english: and yet it stops harmful winds and dews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and concludes a teaching earlier about the meaning of waving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even non-essential parts of a מצוה protect against calamity, as proven by תנופה.

steps.title: רבא applies this to the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the same protective idea applies to waving the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The same is true with the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא extends the idea from the offering to the לולב: waving the לולב also holds back harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waving the לולב is also not the core of the מצוה, since the core is simply picking it up. Still, one should wave it, because it carries the same protective power as תנופה.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm branch taken on סוכות together with the other species

phrases.english: And Rava said: And likewise with the lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the protective principle of תנופה to the לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should wave the לולב, since this too holds back harm.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב calls his waving an arrow at the שטן
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב would wave the לולב back and forth and declare that it was an arrow in the eye of the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב would move the לולב away and bring it back, and say: This is an arrow in the eye of the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports the personal practice of רב אחא בר יעקב while waving. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will judge that practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He saw his waving as a victory over the שטן: despite the שטן's efforts, the Jews keep doing מצוות with joy. He said this out loud as a kind of triumphant declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: He would move it away and bring it back (waving)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov
would move it out and bring it back,
and say: This is an arrow in the eye of the Satan.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מַמְטֵי לֵיהּ וּמַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of an Amora waving the לולב with a protective intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא בר יעקב treated waving the לולב as a weapon against the שטן.

steps.title: Such a declaration is unwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אחא's declaration, because it provokes the שטן to come after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not a proper thing to do, because the שטן will come to stir up trouble against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אחא's saying: waving is good, but announcing victory over the שטן is a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taunting the שטן invites him to try harder to make the person sin. The גמרא rejects only the declaration, not the waving itself.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not a proper thing (to do)
To provoke or incite against him

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not criticizing waving the לולב. It is only criticizing the boastful words.

phrases.english: But that is not a proper thing,
because he (the Satan) will come to provoke him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practice described in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אחא's verbal declaration, not the act of waving.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Taunting the שטן provokes him to attack the person spiritually.
steps.whatToRemember: Waving the לולב protects, like תנופה does, but one should not boast about defeating the שטן.

steps.title: משנה: taking the לולב at home or later in the day
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a traveler without a לולב takes it at his table when he gets home, and one who missed the morning takes it in the afternoon, since the whole day is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who was traveling and did not have a לולב with him to take: when he enters his house, he should take it at his table. If he did not take it in the morning, he should take it in the afternoon, because the entire day is valid for the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives two rules about the timing of the לולב: take it at home, even at the table, and if you missed the morning, the afternoon still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule implies that one takes the לולב even in the middle of a meal. The second rule sets the time for the מצוה as the whole day, not only the morning. The גמרא will now examine how these two rules fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: At his table, i.e., during his meal

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the source for the halacha that the whole day is valid for taking the לולב.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who was coming on the road
and did not have a lulav in his hand to take,
when he enters his house, he should take it at his table.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָטַל שַׁחֲרִית — יִטּוֹל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם,
phrases.english: If he did not take it in the morning, he should take it in the afternoon,
for the whole day is valid for the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְלֹא הָיָה בְּיָדוֹ לוּלָב לִיטּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic: the timing of taking the לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One takes the לולב at one's table upon arriving home, and the whole day is valid for the מצוה.

steps.title: Must he interrupt his meal? A contradiction from the prayer rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'at his table' as requiring one to stop his meal. That contradicts a משנה stating that if people have begun eating, they do not stop for תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said he takes it at his table. Does that mean he interrupts his meal? But a contradiction was raised: if they already started, they do not interrupt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה (one interrupts a meal for the לולב) and then sets it against another משנה that says one does not interrupt a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה (שבת ט:) teaches that one who has begun a meal does not stop to daven מנחה. Our משנה seems to say the opposite: stop the meal for the לולב. So the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
That is to say / does this imply
And they contrasted it: introduces a contradiction from another source

phrases.english: GEMARA:
You said: he takes it at his table;
is that to say that he interrupts (his meal)?
But a contradiction was raised:
If they started, they do not interrupt!
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in שבת ט:, about davening מנחה after you've already started a meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה's first clause and challenges it from an outside source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from our משנה that one must interrupt a meal to take the לולב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה rules that one who has begun a meal does not interrupt it (for תפילה), which suggests that one should not interrupt for the לולב either.

steps.title: רב ספרא: it depends on whether time remains
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that one interrupts only when there will be no time left in the day; when there is time, one does not interrupt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: It is not difficult. This case is where there is still time in the day; that case is where there is no time left in the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא resolves the contradiction by dividing the cases according to how much of the day is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'do not interrupt' (the תפילה source) applies when there is still enough time to do the מצוה after the meal. Our משנה, which requires interrupting for the לולב, is talking about a case where the day is about to end. If he waited, he would miss the מצוה completely.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

phrases.english: Rav Safra said: It is not difficult;
this is where there is time left in the day,
phrases.notes: So there's no need to interrupt, just like in the case about תפילה.

phrases.english: that is where there is no time left in the day.
phrases.notes: He must interrupt, as in our משנה about the לולב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to give opposite rules for the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: They describe different situations: interrupt only when no time remains, otherwise do not.

steps.title: רבא: there was never a real contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the question was weak from the start: the לולב is a מצוה דאורייתא and תפילה is only דרבנן, so they can easily have different rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps this one is from the Torah, and that one is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not attack רב ספרא's answer. He attacks the question itself, saying the two sources were never comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Interrupting a meal for a Torah מצוה (the לולב) makes sense, while for a rabbinic obligation (תפילה) one need not stop. Since the two cases differ in level, there is no contradiction to resolve, and רב ספרא's answer becomes unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (dismissing a question)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is rejecting the question (the קשיא), not offering another answer to it. That is why he then goes on to propose a different question.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps this (lulav) is Torah law, and that (prayer) is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: תפילה is considered דרבנן in this context.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the whole קשיא of step 6, which makes רב ספרא's answer unnecessary.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The original contradiction between our משנה and the תפילה משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It compares a Torah מצוה with a rabbinic one, and these can naturally have different rules about interrupting.

steps.title: רבא's real question: the משנה contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא proposes the true difficulty: the first clause implies interrupting the meal, but the second clause (the whole day is valid) implies there is no need to interrupt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty. 'When he enters his house he takes it at his table', so apparently he interrupts. And then it teaches: 'If he did not take it in the morning, he takes it in the afternoon', so apparently he does not interrupt!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the outside contradiction with an internal one, setting the two halves of our own משנה against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, 'take it at his table', suggests stopping the meal. The second clause says that the whole day is valid and one can push the לולב off until the afternoon, which suggests there is no urgency to interrupt. So the משנה seems inconsistent with itself, and the answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the formula רבא uses to redirect a sugya: drop a weak question and put forward the sharper one that really needs an answer.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
If there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
'When he enters his house, he takes it at his table',
apparently he interrupts;
and then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָטַל שַׁחֲרִית — יִטּוֹל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם.
phrases.english: 'If he did not take it in the morning, he takes it in the afternoon',
apparently he does not interrupt!
phrases.notes: Since there is plenty of time, he can finish eating first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אִי קַשְׁיָא — הָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After dismissing the outside contradiction, רבא raises an internal contradiction within the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency between the משנה's first clause and its second clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause implies one must interrupt the meal, while the second clause's 'whole day is valid' implies one need not interrupt.

steps.title: רב ספרא: It Depends on Whether Time Is Left in the Day
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא resolves רבא's contradiction. The first clause, which says to interrupt the meal, is when no time will be left in the day. The second clause, which says the whole day is valid, is when there is still time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: It is not difficult. This clause is where there is still time in the day. That clause is where there is no time left in the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers רבא's question from step 9 about the two halves of the משנה seeming to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked how the משנה can say both 'interrupt your meal' and 'the whole day is valid.' רב ספרא splits the cases. If the day is about to end, you must stop eating and take the לולב. If there is still plenty of time, you may finish eating and take it later.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is a standard opening for an answer.
This one... that one. Used to split two sources into two different cases.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said: It is not difficult.
This clause is where there is still time in the day,
phrases.notes: In this case there is no need to interrupt the meal.

phrases.english: that clause is where there is no time left in the day.
phrases.notes: In this case one must interrupt the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's internal contradiction from step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses of the משנה seem to give opposite instructions about interrupting the meal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each clause applies to a different situation: no time left versus time remaining.

steps.title: רבי זירא: The Two Clauses Never Clashed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says רבא's question was not a real problem. The משנה could mean it is a מצוה to interrupt the meal, but if someone did not interrupt, he can still take the לולב in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps it is a מצוה to interrupt. If he did not interrupt, he should take it in the afternoon, because the whole day is valid for the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects רבא's question from step 9, so רב ספרא's answer is not even needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא reads the two clauses as two levels, not a contradiction. Stopping to take the לולב is the ideal way. But if a person kept eating, he has not lost the מצוה, because he can still fulfill it later that day.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? This means the question is not really a problem.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps it is a מצוה to interrupt the meal,
phrases.notes: This is the ideal way to act.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא פְּסַיק — יִטּוֹל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם,
phrases.english: but if he did not interrupt, he should take it in the afternoon,
for the whole day is valid for the lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the need for רב ספרא's answer by rejecting the question it was answering.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's proposed contradiction between the two clauses of the משנה (step 9)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The clauses can be read as 'ideal' and 'after the fact' (לכתחילה and בדיעבד), so they do not conflict.

steps.title: רבי זירא Restores the Original Question: The Later Days Are Only Rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא goes back to the original contradiction between לולב and תפילה. He answers רבא's objection by saying the משנה is talking about the days after the first day, when the לולב is only a rabbinic מצוה, just like תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: Really, it is as we said at first. And as for what bothered you, that one is from the Torah and the other is rabbinic: here we are dealing with the second day of the festival, which is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings back the first question from step 6 and answers רבא's objection from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said לולב and תפילה are not comparable, because one is from the Torah and the other is rabbinic. רבי זירא answers that our משנה is about the later days of סוכות. On those days, taking the לולב outside the מקדש is only a rabbinic מצוה. So both are rabbinic, the original contradiction is a real question again, and רב ספרא's original answer from step 7 (interrupt only when no time is left in the day) resolves it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. Used to return to an earlier position.
Here it means the days after the first day of סוכות.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יום טוב שני' does not mean the extra day of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל. It means the days after the first day of סוכות. On those days, taking the לולב outside the מקדש is only a rabbinic מצוה. Only the first day is from the Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Torah-level לולב obligation outside the מקדש applies only on the first day. That fact shapes many laws about the לולב.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
Actually, it is as we said at first,
phrases.notes: The original contradiction between לולב and תפילה stands, and so does רב ספרא's answer to it.

phrases.english: and as for what was difficult for you,
that this one is Torah law and that one is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: This was רבא's objection in step 8.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי דְּרַבָּנַן עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: here we are dealing with the second day of the festival, which is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְאָמְרִינַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's new question, רבי זירא returns to the original question and defends it against רבא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the משנה is about the rabbinic days
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לולב is from the Torah and תפילה is rabbinic, so they cannot be compared.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the later days, when the לולב is rabbinic. So the comparison to תפילה is valid, and רב ספרא's distinction about time left in the day resolves it.

steps.title: Proof from the Wording: A Traveler Cannot Be on the First Day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי זירא from the משנה's words 'one who was coming on the road.' Traveling is not allowed on the first day of יום טוב, so the משנה must be talking about the later days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also precise, since it teaches: 'One who was coming on the road and has no לולב in his hand.' If you think it is the first day of יום טוב, is that allowed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the משנה's own wording to support רבי זירא's claim in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes someone traveling on the road. Long-distance travel is forbidden on the first day of יום טוב. So this case must be on a later day, which is exactly the rabbinic day רבי זירא described.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise. The wording itself supports this reading.
From the fact that it teaches
It enters your mind, if you think

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the traveler with no לולב is talking about the later, rabbinic days of סוכות. That is why it can be compared to the rule for תפילה.

phrases.english: It is also precise, from the fact that it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁבָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאֵין בְּיָדוֹ לוּלָב.
phrases.english: One who was coming on the road and has no lulav in his hand.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that this is the first day of the festival,
is it permitted?!
phrases.notes: Traveling a long way is forbidden on the first day of יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's case definition from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה is talking about the later, rabbinic days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'מי שבא בדרך,' a traveler, which cannot describe the first day of יום טוב

steps.title: New משנה: When Someone Else Leads You in Hallel
steps.stepSummary: If an עבד, אשה, or קטן recites הלל for a man, he must repeat every word after them, and a curse should come on him for not knowing it himself. If an adult man recites it for him, he only answers 'הללויה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone for whom a slave, a woman, or a minor was reciting הלל repeats after them what they say, and may a curse come to him. If an adult was reciting it for him, he answers 'הללויה' after him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how a person fulfills הלל when someone else is leading it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד, אשה, or קטן is not obligated in הלל the way an adult man is. So they cannot fulfill it for him, and he must say every word himself. An adult man who is obligated can fulfill it for him, so the listener only needs to answer 'הללויה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Recite for him, leading him in the text
הללויה, the response said after each line of הלל

steps.confusionAlert: The curse is not because of the person reading. It is on the listener, for being so ignorant that he needs someone who is not obligated to read הלל for him.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה עֶבֶד אוֹ אִשָּׁה אוֹ קָטָן מַקְרִין אוֹתוֹ —
phrases.english: One for whom a slave, a woman, or a minor was reciting (hallel),
repeats after them what they are saying,
phrases.notes: Word for word, because they cannot fulfill it for him.

phrases.english: and may a curse come to him.
If an adult was reciting it for him,
he answers after him 'Halleluyah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיָה עֶבֶד אוֹ אִשָּׁה אוֹ קָטָן מַקְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, reciting הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If someone not obligated leads הלל, the listener repeats every word. If an obligated adult leads, the listener only answers הללויה.

steps.title: Hallel Follows Local Custom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that repeating verses, saying them only once, and saying a ברכה on הלל all follow the custom of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where they are used to repeating, he repeats. Where they say it plainly, he says it plainly. Where they bless, he blesses. Everything follows the custom of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and says that the details of how הלל is recited depend on the local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some places repeated certain verses of הלל, and some said each verse only once. Some said a ברכה on it and some did not. The משנה does not pick one way. It tells each person to follow the custom of where he is.
steps.whatToRemember: How הלל is said, whether with repeated verses or a ברכה, follows the local מנהג.

phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed to repeat, he should repeat;
to say it plainly, he should say it plainly;
to recite a blessing, he should recite a blessing;
everything follows the custom of the place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with rules about the form of הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating verses, saying them plainly, and saying a ברכה on הלל all follow local custom.

steps.title: A son, slave, or wife may bless on a man's behalf, but he is cursed for needing it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a son, a slave, and a wife can say a ברכה on a man's behalf. The חכמים still curse a man who depends on his wife and children for this. The final words, 'אמר רבא', introduce the next statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: In truth they said that a son may say a ברכה on behalf of his father, a slave on behalf of his master, and a wife on behalf of her husband. But the חכמים said: May a curse come upon a man whose wife and children have to say the ברכה for him. רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a ברייתא that matches the משנה's curse on a man who needs others to say הלל for him. The last words, 'אמר רבא', set up a new statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes two separate points. First, the halacha: a son, slave, or wife can say the ברכה for a man, and he is יוצא. Second, the value judgment: it is a disgrace for a man not to know the ברכה himself, so he deserves a curse. This lines up with the משנה in Step 14, where a man is cursed if he relies on an עבד, אשה, or קטן to say הלל for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In truth they said.' A phrase that signals an accepted, established הלכה.
Saying a ברכה on behalf of someone else, so that the listener fulfills his obligation.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not contradict itself. The first half says the ברכה works, so the man does fulfill his obligation. The second half says it is shameful that he did not know it himself. Both halves are true at once.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא explains the משנה's curse. The curse does not mean the man failed to fulfill the מצוה. It is a rebuke for being ignorant.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: The גמרא section begins, opening with a ברייתא.

phrases.english: In truth they said
phrases.notes: This marks an established, accepted rule.

phrases.english: a son may say a blessing on behalf of his father,
and a slave may say a blessing on behalf of his master,
and a woman may say a blessing on behalf of her husband,
but the Sages said:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא turns from the halacha to a rebuke.

phrases.english: May a curse come upon a man
whose wife and children say the blessing for him.
phrases.notes: He needs them because he never learned the ברכה himself.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: This introduces רבא's statement, which continues on the next amud. It is not part of the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ בֵּן מְבָרֵךְ לְאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the גמרא on the משנה. The ברייתא parallels and reinforces the משנה's curse from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son, a slave, or a wife may say a ברכה on a man's behalf, and he is יוצא. Even so, a man who depends on them because he does not know the ברכה deserves a curse.
